minutes.headline: Committee begins staged process to decide whether to renovate or replace Turkey Hill Elementary, no vote yet
minutes.summary: This School Committee meeting covered routine business (transfers, donations, minutes) and the superintendent's report before moving into an extended discussion of long-term facilities planning. The bulk of the meeting was a debate over how to decide the future of Turkey Hill Elementary (renovate vs. rebuild) and how MSBA reimbursement works, ending with an agreed staged process rather than a decision; the committee also took first readings of four policies and heard a Trust Fund Commission chairman ask that all school-related gift/trust records be turned over for review.

what_happened.line: The committee agreed to a staged, multi-meeting process for deciding whether to renovate or replace Turkey Hill Elementary, starting with building needs before cost or funding options.
Rather than have the facilities director attend the next meeting, the committee will first collect written feedback from Turkey Hill staff on what the building needs.

The committee took first readings on four policies -- advertising in schools, a Monty Tech pathway program, cashless payment at events, and competency determination -- and sent each to a second reading.

The Trust Fund Commission's chairman told the committee that school-related gifts and trusts are town property under statute and asked that scholarship and donor records be turned over to the treasurer's office for review.
The committee approved routine items: two line-item transfers, four donations, and a new scholarship named for James J. Larkin.

why_it_matters: The renovate-versus-rebuild choice for Turkey Hill will eventually come before residents as a building project and a tax question, and how much the state's MSBA program reimburses depends on which path the committee picks.

The four policies now headed to a second reading -- including cashless payment at school events -- will return for further debate before they take effect, and could change how families pay for or access school activities.
A request to catalog school-related trusts and scholarships touches funds set aside for student scholarships and could affect who has authority to approve them.
